did_you_know.text: Did you know? Boaz met the redeemer at the city gate, which was a place of public assembly, and addressed him as “So-and-so” instead of mentioning his name.
Did you know? Boaz invited ten of the city’s elders to sit there so they could witness the conversation and the decision concerning the redemption.
Did you know? At first, the redeemer agreed to redeem Elimelech’s parcel of land, but later withdrew when it became clear that the redemption also included Ruth.
Did you know? Boaz explained that the transaction included not only the field but also Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon’s wife, in order to preserve the name of the deceased on his inheritance.
Did you know? According to the account in this chapter, removing a sandal and giving it to another person served in Israel as a confirmation and witness of a redemption and transfer transaction.
Did you know? The people and the elders blessed Boaz and Ruth by invoking Rachel and Leah, who built the house of Israel, and Tamar, who bore Perez to Judah.
Did you know? After Boaz took Ruth as his wife, the text says that the Lord enabled her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son.
Did you know? The women who lived there named the child Obed, and the text directly connects him to Jesse and David: Obed was the father of Jesse, and Jesse was the father of David.
Did you know? The Book of Ruth ends with a genealogy leading from Perez through Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon, Boaz, and Obed to Jesse and David.
